summary: File the participial example under Part. Pass., retaining a single copy.
before: d-owe-le tre=farxe, qḏole d-u=zʕuro nqíwo-yo w d-i=barṯo d-lo nqówo-yo
after: d-owe-le tre=farxe, qḏole d-u=zʕuro nqíwo-yo w d-i=barṯo d-lo nqówo-yo
rationale: The relevant forms nqíwo-yo and nqówo-yo are participles with the copula, describing whether the neck is perforated. There is no infinitive of nqw in this example. The same quotation and references already occur in nqw’s Part. Pass. box (nqw.I.d.part-pass.1); merge with that existing copy rather than creating a duplicate.

summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 55/3)

data.turoyo: <...> Aṯi. Mərralle laḥ ḥəyewən, əmmi: "Axile lu qaġo šwaʕ freḏe, heš klən b feme. Omər Oḏəm: "Mənqowo i qərrəkayḏe, nufli li arʕo. <...>
data.translation: <...> Als er zurückkam, sagten ihm die Tiere: "Der Rabe hat sieben Körner gefressen, noch sind sie in seinem Munde." Da sprach Adam: "Seine Kehle soll durchbohrt sein und die Körner sollen zu Boden fallen." <...>

rationale: Adds absent Detransitive Infectum; the curse gives a prospective agentless piercing result, unlike following result-state forms.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.20/3855)

data.turoyo: Bu Sayfo nquwwolle ad dəkoṯo lə ḥḏoḏe, xrəmiwonne. Nəfqiwo bi xaṣrayo, uzzənwo bayo. <...>
data.translation: In the Sayfo they had bored through the places to one another, they used to pierce them through. They would emerge on this side, go through that one. <...>

rationale: New active Preterit-wa1 box; linking places by bored passages supports round-1 tunnelling gloss.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) durchlöchert werden, durchlöchert sein, voller Löcher sein

data.gloss: (Detrans.) durchlöchert werden, durchlöchert sein, voller Löcher sein

rationale: Explicit counterpart of active I.1, already implicit in inherited Detransitive Preterit and Part. Pass.; the newly attested Infectum curse supplies the prospective event beside the state.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 3.2/25)

data.turoyo: <...> kətwole ṣʕuno, bu ṣʕunawo nqule i xaṣrayo w hayo diḏe w maḥatlele ḥuṭo w bu ṣʕunawo šutanwo maye, huwe w i Wardo d bə Čalma.
data.translation: <...> (Mein Großvater) hatte einen Schuh, in diesen Schuh bohrte er auf beiden Seiten ein Loch, befestigte eine Schnur daran, und aus diesem Schuh tranken sie Wasser, er und die Wardo d-bĭ-Čalma.

rationale: Thin active Preterit I.1 cell; explicit shoe and side-parts provide a new independent piercing context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (LuF 3/7)

data.turoyo: <...> Kəmmi, koməḥyo ruḥa bu isan, konəqwole, xd u buġro di  tfənge. Kəmmi, konəqwo u ǧəsmo du isan <...>
data.translation: <...> Man sagt, sie wirft sich auf den Menschen und durchbohrt ihn wie eine Flintenkugel, durchbohrt den Leib des Menschen. <...>

rationale: Better-context extension of the inherited short snake quotation: includes additional nominal body object beside -le. The existing first clause is quoted only as necessary context for the new second target.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Sterka Zera/29)

data.turoyo: <...> Əmmo, ‘Ha kal koḥozat, hǎka dəmṭutu aʕ-ʕašfe w am-maḏ̣răbat, w am-maqrasyoṯe, nuqwutu u-naqwano, dkətyo hawxa čike rabo w guršūtli — naxwa čara layto.’
data.translation: <...> She said, ‘Hey, you see, if you bring hoes and hammers and chisels, and make this hole, which has to be a bit large like so, and pull me out ... otherwise there is no way.’

rationale: Thin active Infectum I.1 cell; cognate hole object with a specified size and rescue purpose.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/93)

data.turoyo: <...> Ḥayṣiwa tre, dəmmat, ḥădī́d aw be mən kə́twalle, aw nuqwiwa, moḥanwa qayso ebe, ínaqqa dlatwalle ḥadī́d. <...>
data.translation: <...> They would fasten two, you might say, iron or whatever they had, or they would bore it, put a piece of wood in it, if they had no iron. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.1 cell; craftsman bores an understood wooden component to replace iron fastening.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/94)

data.turoyo: Breše di+mašono nuqwíwayle tre+naqwe, u+qayso hawxa ḥlímoyo, i+mašono d̥kəmmina, hawxa yarəxto masərto b̥áṯeyo, tre tloṯo+naqwe nuqwíwayla. <...>
data.translation: In the head of the shaft, they would bore two holes in it, the wood is so thick, the shaft, let’s say, is so long tied to this one, they would bore two-three holes in it. <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa I.1 cell; two tokens contrast component suffixes -le/-la with explicit cognate result objects, retained once.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 5.2/55)

data.turoyo: <...> komər ʕarqəwone sligi, nqiwi haqqas həngi kmoḥe raġloṯe bak kefe, yaʕni səsyo yo kmaqləʕ <...>
data.translation: <...> Seine Fersen wurden abgeschabt, sie wurden eingedellt, so stark schlug er seine Füße an die Steine, als ob es ein Pferd wäre, das er antreibt. <...>

rationale: Thin Detransitive Preterit cell; narrative damage to heels, an affected-surface extension rather than an invented denting sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (JTM 1.1/24)

data.turoyo: <...> Mənayye kowən kaḥkune, gawayye nqiwe, w mənayye kowən kəmmənne luwašat, ksaymi čəzeġi bənne. <...>
data.translation: <...> Manche davon werden zu Kringeln geformt, die in der Mitte ein Loch haben, und andere zu Fladenbroten, die man mit eingeritzten Strichen verziert. <...>

rationale: Third Detransitive Part. Pass. example; bread centres have holes, with no agent in the state predicate.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (MAC Ishaq Material culture/70)

data.turoyo: <...> Kefe nqiwe, šriqe, məqqa dhowən... hawxa dlowən ġắlabe šafire ŭ msawye ṭawtərne, lăǧan dzəbṭi ḥḏoḏe, dməsnodi ləḥḏoḏe, ʕam i+čmənto.
data.translation: <...> Pierced stones, hollow stones, however much (abraded) they may be, so, if they aren’t very beautiful and level, they’re better, so they catch each other, lean against each other, with the cement.

rationale: Fourth Detransitive Part. Pass. example; natural porous building stones show that a prior drilling event is not entailed.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (1/45)

data.turoyo: At taxtayat du madbax, me d kətwayye nqiwe w fayite, aʕ ʕubbugre ʕəbriwo, əxliwo am muklone.
data.translation: Da die dielen der Küche voller Löcher und brüchig waren, kamen die Ratten herein und fraßen die Speisen auf.

rationale: Fifth Detransitive Part. Pass. example; plural kitchen boards and a causal clause contrast with the inherited singular roof.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (PrS 55/3)

data.turoyo: <...> Mu yawmo d məlle l Oḏəm, nqiwo i qərrəke du qaġo w uʕdo m aloho nquto yo, koxəl šawʕo faqe, knofəl əšto, kfoyəš ḥa, knoḥət l gawe. <...>
data.translation: <...> Von dem Tage an, wo Adam dies gesagt hat, ist die Kehle des Raben durchbohrt, bis auf den heutigen Tage durch göttliche Fügung; wenn er sieben Happen isst, fallen sechs zu Boden und einer nur bleibt ihm und geht in den Magen hinab. <...>

rationale: Unusual agreement and explicit divine-source exception beyond the filled cell: masculine-shaped nqiwo and feminine nquto share the throat referent, and m aloho may mark source or agent.

summary: All 27 full occurrences were reviewed. The active meaning is piercing/boring an affected surface, with an already inherited tunnelling extension now included in the gloss.

Craft examples have an understood wood patient or a component suffix -le/-la together with tre naqwe as cognate result object. nuqwutu u-naqwano enlarges an opening for rescue; these remain I.1, not separate technical senses.

Detransitive Preterit describes a resistant sword or narrative heel damage; Detransitive Infectum Mənqowo in Adam's curse is prospective. The following nqiwo/nquto and predicative -yo describe persistent result or property states.
At PrS 55/3 preposed nqiwo with feminine throat contrasts with agreeing nquto; m aloho can be source/cause or agent and is not forced into one category.

The same raven-offspring sentence legitimately contains two targets: Part. Pass. nqiwo and privative nqowo under the inherited Detransitive Infinitiv. A shared sentence is not by itself a duplicated form entry; preserve both filings pending morphological review.
Source spelling nqula in 95/249 and nqiwi in 61/369 remain visible as unresolved agreement/form questions. No silent repairs or new paradigms are introduced.
Existing examples cited by old prs page/line references recur under supplied PrS text/verse numbering. These matches are not automatically new attestations or proven citation errors.
No fixed idiom or light-verb construction is established by these occurrences. Permitted nuqw and Mənqowo lookup checks support cross-checking the family, not new unrelated roots.
All three Jan records checked. nquwwolle adds active Preterit-wa; keep source ww and its l-agent morphology rather than silently normalising it.

Round 1 already widens active1 to tunnelling and adds a Detransitive gloss. Jan does not require those proposals again. Existing Detransitive Part. Pass.1 has six cumulative examples, so neither hollow ground nor the rock-name gloss is added for thin-cell reasons.
nqiwo with yo profiles a resulting/spatial property; nqəwto modifies Kefo in a place-name gloss. Neither requires a new event of deliberate boring.
lə ḥḏoḏe marks the mutually connected locations in the active passage example, not human reciprocal agents. English is the supplied project machine translation.
Confirm Detransitive Infectum Mənqowo at PrS 55/3: segmentation and vocalism, and contrast with the subsequent persistent-state forms.
Is preposed nqiwo before feminine qərrəke invariant, dialectal agreement, or an edition error? Confirm subsequent feminine nquto without normalizing the source.
Does m aloho in the same verse mark the agent of the state or its divine source/cause?
Is dlo nqowo genuinely privative Detransitive Infinitiv, as the glossary files it, or a vocalic variant of the Part. Pass.? The shared sentence alone cannot decide.
Reconcile old prs 90/10,132/29,132/32,151/27 with supplied PrS 35/28,47/17,47/19,55/3; preserve numbering systems until their relationship is verified.
At 61/369 does nqiwi denote bodily sores or torn clothing at the loins, and is it Detransitive Preterit or Part. Pass.?
At 95/249 is nqula a source error for nqulan, or does it encode another subject? The unusual-form proposal is withheld.
At PrS 47/17 is the agent Hasan or the awl? The German dieser alone cannot resolve the Turoyo suffix.
At 72/5 is -le resumptive of the opening or a beneficiary? Existing form filing is preserved.
Confirm adjacent šriqe in MAC Material culture/70; no productive root or new nqw sense is inferred from its English hollow gloss.
Confirm segmentation and person/object values of nquwwolle at 2.20/3855; the active Preterit-wa analysis is provisional but supported by the l-agent ending and retrospective narrative.
Does nqiwo at 1.8/295 mean naturally hollow, tunnelled or perforated substrate? No man-made excavation is inferred from that state alone.
Affected surfaces range from metal and a shoe to heels and horse flanks. Bodily damage does not yet justify a separate denting or wounding sense.
Holey bread and naturally porous stones are properties; the form does not require an earlier drilling event.

Jan supports round 1’s excavation/tunnelling clarification through passages linking cavities. Hollow ground and a pierced-rock place-name repeat the already documented Detransitive property of porous material.
